title: Migrate CI to hermetic root images + distributed remote build cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Replace the current layered Docker inheritance approach with a set of hermetic root base images and enable a distributed BuildKit remote cache (s3+cache-proxy) to reduce CI build times and flakiness. This ticket covers base image consolidation, cache priming strategy, Buildx invocation standardization, and a small toolchain audit (linters/Node/Golang) to ensure reproducible artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: CI median cold build time reduced by >=40% for core repo compared to 2026-01 baseline
Cache hit rate >= 70% for daily commits after two weeks of priming
All major pipelines use hermetic base images (no ad-hoc FROM lines to upstream images)
Build artifacts are bit-for-bit reproducible for deterministic steps (where applicable)
No increase in CI cost per successful build > 5% during rollout window
Rollforward/rollback documented and tested (can revert to previous images and cache policy)
plan: Phase 1: Audit (1 week) — enumerate Dockerfiles, identify bespoke FROM layers, capture current layering metadata and average layer sizes

Phase 2: Build hermetic root images (2 weeks) — create minimal root images per language runtime (node:18-prod, go:1.20-prod, python:3.11-prod) with pinned system packages and tooling; publish to private registry with content-addressable tags
Phase 3: Remote cache infra (1 week) — deploy s3-backed BuildKit cache and a cache-proxy (telemetry + eviction policy), integrate with existing CI runners
Phase 4: CI job standardization (1 week) — rework build scripts to use buildx bake, enable inline --cache-from/--cache-to and use priming steps for daily warmup
Phase 5: Toolchain audit (1 week) — upgrade eslint/tsc/golangci-lint versions in a controlled rollout, fix top-priority linter regressions
Phase 6: Rollout & monitoring (2 weeks) — enable for low-risk pipelines, measure hit rates and build times, iterate on cache TTL and priming cadence
Phase 7: Full rollout and cleanup (1 week) — migrate remaining repos, deprecate legacy base images, update docs
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Completed initial Dockerfile inventory across 42 repos (spreadsheet link). Identified 9 repos with non-standard base layering causing high churn.

2026-02-19: Built PoC hermetic node:18-prod image with pinned apt packages and yarn 1.22; published to internal registry (registry.redwood.local/ci/node:18-prod). PoC reduced cold build step by ~38% in sample repo.
2026-02-24: Deployed BuildKit cache proxy to staging using s3://redwood-ci-cache (lifecycle 30d). Configured eviction policy: LRU with 10GB per repo namespace.
2026-03-03: Standardized buildx invocation and bake file in core-repo; enabled --cache-from/--cache-to with manifest lists. First 5 pipelines moved to cache show 63% hit rate after 5 days of priming.
2026-03-08: Ran initial golangci-lint upgrade in infra repo; fixed top-10 issues and added suppressed rules for legacy generated code. No CI noise observed after fixes.
review_feedback: PM review (Priya Shah): please include cost guardrails and CI budget alerting during rollout — added monitoring hooks
Security (Jordan Patel): request to run SBOM generation for new base images and store in compliance bucket — agreed, SBOM step added to image build pipeline
Platform eng (Maya Chen): suggested adding cache namespace per-commit-hash for PR builds to avoid cross-PR pollution — implemented as a prefixed namespace in bake configs
Devex (Ethan Ross): recommended example repo templates and migration checklist for 3rd-party integrations — drafting templates
risks: Cache poisoning between PRs if namespaces are misconfigured — mitigated by per-PR namespace scheme and short TTL for PR caches
Unexpected package incompatibilities when moving to pinned system packages in hermetic images — mitigated by running smoke suites in staging images
Temporary increase in S3 costs during priming window — will monitor and cap priming concurrency
Rollout could surface flaky tests that were previously masked by slower builds — decouple failure root-cause tracking and add test-heatmap
test_plan: Create canary pipeline for low-traffic repo and run N=50 builds comparing old vs new images
Automated verification step: validate artifact checksums and SBOM presence after image-based builds
Expose cache metrics (hit/miss) to Console dashboard and alert if hit_rate < 50% after 7 days
Manual rollback drill: revert bake to old base image and validate build run within 30 minutes
notes: Primary goal is developer productivity and predictable build economics. We intentionally keep hermetic images minimal to reduce CVE surface and expedite scanning. Post-rollout, we expect ~30-45% aggregate CI time savings and clearer deterministic builds for release engineering.
